name: house-hunt
//: The workspace root. It owns the checks that span packages and the tooling every package shares; each app owns its own build.

scripts.//package: Vercel builds only apps/web and cannot build the extension, so the download served by the Install tab is a committed asset and `package` writes it directly. There was a second script that copied it into place; nobody ran it, which is how the served zip stayed at 0.1.0 for three versions.
scripts.check:all: pnpm check && pnpm check:sync && pnpm check:functions && pnpm check:one-client && pnpm check:routes && pnpm check:bridge && pnpm check:area && pnpm check:facts && pnpm check:filter && pnpm check:listing && pnpm check:platform && pnpm check:hubs && pnpm check:stage && pnpm check:shortlist && pnpm check:sweep && pnpm check:travel && pnpm check:png && pnpm check:analysis && pnpm check:predict && pnpm check:withdrawn && pnpm check:recheck && pnpm check:full-sweep && pnpm check:zip
scripts.deploy:function: tsx tools/sync-edge-function.ts --check && bash -c 'set -a; source ./.env; set +a; if [ -n "$WEB_APP_ORIGIN" ]; then supabase secrets set WEB_APP_ORIGIN="$WEB_APP_ORIGIN" --project-ref "$SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF" || exit 1; else echo "warning: WEB_APP_ORIGIN unset in .env — unsetting any existing secret so CORS does not keep allowing a stale origin" >&2; supabase secrets unset WEB_APP_ORIGIN --project-ref "$SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; for fn in analyse invite listing resolve-location travel; do supabase functions deploy "$fn" --project-ref "$SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF" || exit 1; done; supabase functions deploy password --project-ref "$SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF" --no-verify-jwt'
